newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland talks chairman Mitchell hails truce.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland talks chairman Mitchell hails truce.

text.p: The chairman of slow-moving Northern Ireland peace talks, former U.S. senator George Mitchell, said on Saturday that he welcomed the IRA truce.

"It continues to be my hope that all parties will join in inclusive, meaningful negotiation to bring about what the people of Northern Ireland want: peace, political stability and reconciliation," he said in a statement.
Mitchell, appointed by Britain and Ireland to chair what they say is the best hope of peace for a generation, added: "I will do all I can to make that possible".

Mitchell has voiced exasperation at the slow pace of the talks he leads and has called on parties taking part to get down to substantive issues without delay or risk losing all confidence from the Northern Ireland people.

The idea of parallel decommissioning - the surrender of IRA arms as the talks progress - was a proposal by Mitchell and his aides to break a 1994/5 deadlock over how armed groups would hand over their weapons.

The proposal finally clinched the second Irish Republican Army truce after Britain and Ireland said they would support it and would not insist on arms being handed over when Sinn Fein joins the negotiations.
